children: Micron plans up to four DRAM fabs in Clay, NY; construction started with initial pour. First plant may begin production in 2030+. Capex guided ~$11.5B Q1 and ~$25B H1 FY2027.
Micron (MU) posted record quarterly revenue of $54.23B driven by AI memory demand and guided next-quarter revenue of $61.5B, signaling continued strong demand for AI-related memory.
Micron (MU) approved about $35B in buybacks, with significant repurchases slated to begin around December 9, marking a large-scale repurchase program and planned early-December activity.
Micron (MU) faced a Taoyuan plant one-day warning strike vote over bonuses and profit-sharing; about 1,994 workers supported it. Micron employs ~15,000 in Taiwan and has ~T$1.6T invested.
Micron (MU) signed 16 supply contracts, 14 with explicit pricing metrics. These terms could affect future revenue recognition tied to contract fulfillment and pricing execution.
Micron (MU) will fund expansion at Indium Corp in Rome, NY, and signed a long-term deal for high-purity indium and critical minerals to support U.S. semiconductor production.
Cantor Fitzgerald kept MU overweight with a $2,000 target, citing guidance that memory shortages may last into 2027–28, SCAs possibly covering up to 50% of revenue, and planned buybacks.
Micron Technology (MU) workers demand an 83‑month salary bonus and a permanent plan giving employees 15% of operating profit as quarterly bonuses; they rejected a prior 68‑month offer.
